faq.q: What is an HS code?
faq.a: It is the Harmonized System code, the worldwide classification of goods. It determines the duties, taxes and checks that apply to your product.

faq.q: How do I benefit from a free trade agreement?
faq.a: Your product must meet the agreement's rules of origin, and you must provide the required proof of origin, for example a EUR.1 certificate for the European Union.

faq.q: Which documents do I need to export?
faq.a: At least a commercial invoice, a packing list and a transport document. Depending on the product and the country, you may also need a certificate of origin, a health certificate or a certificate of conformity.

faq.q: Can you help with goods held at customs?
faq.a: Yes, contact us: we analyse the reason for the hold and the missing documents to resolve the situation as quickly as possible.

faq.q: Which Incoterm should I choose for a first export?
faq.a: Often an Incoterm where your responsibility ends early, such as FCA or FOB, to limit risk. The right choice also depends on what your customer can organise: we discuss it with you.

faq.q: Groupage or full container?
faq.a: For small volumes, groupage (LCL) shares a container among several shippers. Above roughly fifteen cubic metres, a full container (FCL) often becomes the better deal.

faq.q: Can goods go to West Africa by road?
faq.a: Yes, road freight is a real option from Morocco to West Africa. We compare it with sea freight based on your goods, lead times and budget.

faq.q: How do I avoid demurrage charges?
faq.a: By preparing the documents before the container arrives and planning its collection. Free days are limited: beyond them, every extra day is charged.

faq.q: What is a letter of credit?
faq.a: It is a commitment by the buyer's bank to pay the seller, provided the seller presents compliant documents on time. It protects both parties.

faq.q: Documentary collection or letter of credit?
faq.a: A documentary collection costs less but does not commit the bank: the buyer can refuse the documents. A letter of credit is safer for the seller, and more expensive.

faq.q: Should I always ask for a deposit?
faq.a: It is not mandatory, but a deposit on order reduces the risk, especially with a new customer.

faq.q: Do you replace a lawyer?
faq.a: No. We prepare the commercial and financial side; for complex legal questions, we refer you to a specialist lawyer.

meta.title: Shipping container guide: dimensions, types and conditions | AFRIEXPORT CONSULTING
meta.description: Dimensions of 20', 40', High Cube, reefer, open top, flat rack and tank containers. Comparison tool, volume calculator and condition guide (new, CW, WWT).

containersPage.title: Everything you need to pick the right container
containersPage.lead: Formats, dimensions, families and conditions: compare shipping containers and estimate in seconds what your goods need.
containersPage.photoAlt: Stacks of yellow and red shipping containers under a blue sky
containersPage.pickerLead: Dry containers carry the vast majority of goods. Choose a format to see its internal dimensions.
containersPage.familiesLead: Each family suits a type of cargo. The right choice avoids extra costs and refusals at loading.

dry.name: Dry
dry.text: The standard container, closed and watertight, for goods with no temperature requirement.
dry.uses: Cartons, pallets, bags, manufactured goods, textiles, materials.
dry.watch: The High Cube version adds 30 cm of height, useful for light, bulky goods.

reefer.name: Reefer
reefer.text: Insulated and fitted with a cooling unit, it keeps a set temperature for the whole voyage.
reefer.uses: Fruit and vegetables, seafood, meat, dairy products, medicines.
reefer.watch: It must be plugged in at the terminal and on board. Goods must be loaded already at the right temperature.

openTop.name: Open Top
openTop.text: With no rigid roof, it is loaded from above by crane and covered with a tarpaulin.
openTop.uses: Machinery, marble and stone, timber, goods too tall for the doors.
openTop.watch: Goods that stick out above the top are "out of gauge": freight is then charged extra.

flatRack.name: Flat Rack
flatRack.text: A reinforced floor with two end walls, no sides and no roof.
flatRack.uses: Machinery, vehicles, coils, steel structures, heavy loads.
flatRack.watch: Lashing must be done by professionals, and the cargo protected from the weather.

tank.name: Tank
tank.text: A stainless steel tank held in a frame with the dimensions of a 20-foot container.
tank.uses: Food-grade liquids, oils, chemicals, hazardous goods.
tank.watch: The tank is usually filled to between 80 and 95% to limit liquid movement in transit.

containersPage.compareLead: Choose two formats: their silhouettes are drawn to the same scale and the differences appear line by line.
containersPage.note: Indicative values: they vary by manufacturer and shipping line. Always check with the carrier before loading.
containersPage.calcLead: Enter the volume, the weight or the number of pallets: we estimate how many containers you need, format by format.

calc.fillHint: A container is rarely filled to 100%: 85% is a prudent assumption.
calc.empty: Fill in at least one field to see the estimate.
calc.note: Indicative estimate. Actual loading depends on packaging, stackability and weight distribution.

containersPage.statesLead: When you buy or lease a container, its condition matters as much as its size. Here are the four grades used in the trade.

states.title: New (One Trip)
states.text: Fresh from the factory, it has made a single voyage, usually from Asia, to be delivered. Flawless look and watertightness.
states.use: Regular exports, storing valuable goods, conversions
states.photoAlt: Doors of recent containers with intact paint

states.title: Cargo Worthy (CW)
states.text: Used, inspected and repaired to IICL standards, it is fit for international ocean shipping, with a valid CSC plate.

states.title: Wind and Watertight (WWT)
states.text: Wind and watertight, but not certified for sea transport. It often has dents and surface rust.

states.title: As Is
states.text: Sold without warranty: it may have holes, stiff doors or a damaged floor. Inspect before you buy.
states.photoAlt: Doors of old containers marked by rust

containersPage.checklistTitle: Checklist before you buy or lease
containersPage.checklistLead: Eight points to check on site, or to have checked by an inspector.

checklist.title: CSC plate
checklist.text: Present, readable and up to date: without it, no ocean shipping.

checklist.title: Container number
checklist.text: Four letters, six digits and a check digit, identical on every side.

checklist.title: Doors and seals
checklist.text: The doors close without force, the gaskets are supple and continuous.

checklist.title: Light test
checklist.text: With the doors closed, no light should get in: otherwise, water will too.

checklist.title: Floor
checklist.text: No broken, soft or oil- or chemical-stained boards.

checklist.title: Rust and dents
checklist.text: Surface rust is normal; rust that goes through is not.

checklist.title: Smell and cleanliness

faq.q: What is the difference between a 40' Dry and a 40' High Cube?
faq.a: Same length and width, but the High Cube is about 30 cm taller. It offers nearly 9 m³ more space, often for similar freight rates.

faq.q: Should I buy or lease a container to export?
faq.a: To ship goods, you usually use the shipping line's container, included in the freight. Buying makes sense for long-term storage or regular shipments to poorly served destinations.

faq.q: What is the CSC plate?
faq.a: It is the safety approval plate required by the International Convention for Safe Containers. It certifies that the container can be handled and stacked safely. Without a valid plate, it cannot travel by sea.

faq.q: What is the VGM?
faq.a: The Verified Gross Mass. Since 2016, the SOLAS convention requires the actual weight of the loaded container to be declared before loading. Without a VGM, the container is not loaded.

faq.q: Can I exceed the stated payload?
faq.a: No. The payload is a technical maximum. You must also respect the road weight limits of every country crossed, which are often lower.
